newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX board to decide on copper warehouse in Chile.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX board to decide on copper warehouse in Chile.

text.p: NYMEX's COMEX copper advisory committee has agreed to move ahead with opening a copper warehouse in Chile, said Neal Wolkoff, a NYMEX board member.
Wolkoff, speaking at American Metal Market's Copper Seminar, said the move needed to be approved by NYMEX's board of directors.
"There is still much work to be done," Wolkoff said. He said the move would be the first toehold for international expansion for an open, transparent copper futures market.
NYMEX was also looking for other delivery points in the Far East, Wolkoff added.

Chile presented special challenges such as tax issues and punitive duties imposed by the U.S. on copper imported from Chile. But high-level government discussions have indicated "that the path will be cleared."
Wolkoff said the U.S. was the world's largest consumer of copper and the world's second-largest producer and should, as a result, have a copper futures market which better reflected this.
Currently, analysts estimate that London Metal Exchange (LME) has well over 90 percent of the world's copper futures market.
Wolkoff noted that most domestically sold copper in the U.S. was priced against COMEX.
NYMEX was angered by LME's decision to open copper warehouses in the U.S.
